messages:
jamie: Noticed an odd correctness window during a multi-tenant shrink: new owner served a key that should've been evicted by a prior demote. Short log: 

```
[2026-07-12T03:22:01Z] demote prefix=acct2/cart epoch=1555 token=hb:7
[2026-07-12T03:22:01Z] evict key=acct2/cart:item99 -> removed
[2026-07-12T03:22:02Z] handback accepted token=hb:7
[2026-07-12T03:22:02Z] read acct2/cart:item99 -> value=present (unexpected)
```

alexa: That implies the evict wasn't durable before handback or the new owner replayed a stale WAL segment. Do we have demote -> durability ordering guaranteed?

tom: Today we try to avoid synchronous flush on demote to keep latency down. Evict tombstones may sit in memtable until compaction. If handback emits token before compaction flush, new owner may never see the tombstone.

neha: Two options: (1) enforce demote durability for eviction markers (append tiny checkpoint) or (2) keep demote fast but attach a "fence_seq" to token so new owner refuses to serve reads below fence until it confirms catch-up. Option (2) is less IO but needs robust fallback.

jamie: Also saw this happen when split+merge churned prefixes; the new owner had a cached snapshot that never saw the tombstone. Fencing would help because cached snapshots would be invalidated until the seq is observed.

alexa: If we choose fencing, the token should include {prefix, last_eviction_seq, wal_offset} signed by old owner. New owner sets prefix state=quarantined until local seq >= last_eviction_seq. During quarantine reads either forward to sequencer or trigger a one-shot delta fetch.

tom: For hot prefixes that causes first-read tail but only briefly. Alternative: pessimistic checkpoint on demote but batch multiple prefix checkpoints into one I/O to amortize cost. We can also rate-limit checkpoint commits during eviction storms.

neha: Implementation plan: prototype token-fence + single-shot delta fetch on first read miss (100ms timeout) + TTL-based forward for rare failures. Add metrics: demote-checkpoint-rate, token-fence-blocks, delta-fetch-latency. Gate behind FF.

ops-bot: Created ticket RM-9009 assigned to tom/neha: "prefix-evict-fence-and-delta-fetch". :white_check_mark:

jamie: I'll file a short RFC with token schema and fallback semantics. Prefer fence+delta for canary; if IO overhead is low we can consider batched checkpointing later.
